One way of achieving this is by using a filter to block parts of the spectrum, calculate the second order light efficiency, and further use this to remove the estimated second order light in all datasets. Here, data from four different filters (two longpass and two shortpass) with three different types of illumination (a radiometric calibration source, cloudy sky and sunny sky) are compared. The short-pass filters used with the sunny sky give best results, while the longpass filters prove useful for validation purposes. A natural light source such as the Sun is shown to be beneficial compared to the calibration source (low intensity in UV) due to differences in spectra from real life measurements.

articleTitle: Corathyp: A New Atmospheric Correction Tool for Satellite Hyperspectral Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Satellite hyperspectral imaging is a fast-growing domain supported by several recently launched satellites (PRISMA, EnMap). Many other missions are planned for the years to come with various improvements such as spatial coverage, revisit or spatial resolution (CHIME, SBG, French hyperspectral mission, etc.). In this context, CORATHYP, a new atmospheric correction code, has been developed in order to extract hyperspectral surface reflectances from satellite measurements, taking advantage of the high spectral resolution for a better characterisation of the atmospheric composition.In CORATHYP, gas concentrations and aerosol properties are first initialized using ECMWF and CAMS data. Then finer water vapour content and aerosol optical thickness are directly retrieved from the acquired image. Afterwards, atmospheric perturbations are corrected to get surface reflectances, by taking into account the scene topography and adjacency effects. All radiative transfer variables are computed by SOS-ABS, a radiative transfer model coupling gas absorption and diffusion, including polarisation effects.

articleTitle: Onboard Hyperspectral Classification Enables Georeferencing
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) has been building a system composed of multiple remote sensing agents for ocean observations. NTNU launched the first HYPerspectral Smallsat for Ocean observation (HYPSO-1) satellite on the 13<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> of January 2022, adding a Hyperspectral Imager satellite to its disposal, while HYPSO-2 will be launched in 2024. However, due to the high dimensionality of the collected data, onboard processing has been introduced on the satellite to potentially deliver information in a more rapid and condensed manner. In this paper, the operational use of onboard classification will be explored, investigating how different algorithms can be applied for data reduction to potentially enable decision-making onboard the satellite such as the use of classified images for onboard georeferencing. The classification could be used to enable near real-time data latency cooperation between the satellite and the other agents, such as autonomous surface vehicles for in-situ measurements.

articleTitle: Triplet-Loss Driven Optimization for Improved Methane Leak Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Methane leaks continue to pose significant threats to the environment, public health, and safety, necessitating more effective detection methods. Building upon our previous work, which utilized one-shot learning for methane leak detection using hyperspectral data, this paper introduces an approach employing triplet loss to further enhance detection accuracy. By leveraging the discriminative power of triplet loss, we establish a robust framework to compare unidentified methane signatures with known methane references. Through extensive evaluation on AVIRIS data from the historic Aliso Canyon methane leak incident, we demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method over traditional one-shot learning techniques. Notably, our approach achieves remarkable gains in both accuracy and speed. By refining the detection process, our study contributes to the advancement of methane leak detection, providing crucial insights for mitigating environmental and public health impacts.

articleTitle: Bayesian Gaussian Process for Correcting Artifacts from Atmospheric Correction and Sensor Noise - A Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Artifacts in hyperspectral images are physically unrealistic values in reflectance spectra, caused either by incorrect estimation of parameters in atmospheric correction or by sensor noise. Atmospheric correction artifacts often appear as excessively high or low values where water has partial absorption. Sensor often appear as single band spikes in spectra. We previously showed that a Gaussian Process trained on library spectra can effectively detect and correct these artifacts. In this paper, we show that correcting for these artifacts can improve processing of the imagery for anomaly detection. Python code for this research shared openly.

articleTitle: Quantitative Assessment of Hayward Kiwi Soluble Solids Content Prediction Using Hyperspectral Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Soluble Solids Content (SSC) of kiwi fruit is an important internal quality attribute that influences its consumption quality and post-harvest shelf life. In this study, a non-invasive measurement and quantitative prediction of SSC indices in Hayward kiwi cultivars was conducted using hyperspectral imaging techniques. Hyperspectral images of 495 kiwi fruits were collected in reflectance mode between the wavelengths of 400 and 1000 nm. This study employed Partial Least Square Regression (PLSR) for calibration and prediction, combined with various preprocessing methods. Amongst, combination of SGS+MSC+PLS obtained better calibration and prediction outcomes, with ${\text{R}}_C^2 = 0.42$, RMSEP = 1.3023 and ${\text{R}}_P^2 = 0.31$, RMSEP = 1.3211 respectively. This study also looked at the feasibility of employing a Moving Window PLSR (MWPLSR) approach to find the best spectral interval and reduce the impact of multicollinearity in the spectral data. Then, MWPLSR approach delivered the best calibration and prediction values in a spectral region spanning 628-947 nm.

articleTitle: Semantic-Guided Point Cloud Upsampling Method for Visual Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Depth acquisition devices can be utilized in visual localization applications to construct an offline database comprised of images and point clouds, thereby facilitating more precise three-dimensional spatial positioning. Yet, the hardware limitations of such depth acquisition devices result in a significantly lower point cloud resolution when compared to the image pixel resolution. Furthermore, the point cloud inevitably contains a certain level of noise generated by environmental factors during the collection process. These factors considerably impede the precision of visual localization. Thus, this paper presents a semantic-guided method for point clouds upsampling. Leveraging the semantic distribution information of the image, this approach upsamples the point cloud data corresponding to pixels containing unique semantic information, providing denser point clouds while eliminating noise. Experimental results demonstrate the successful performance of the proposed approach in point cloud upsampling, thereby effectively enhancing the accuracy of visual localization.

articleTitle: A Dedicated Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification Based on Multi-Objective Evolutionary Search
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Classification of Hyperspectral remote sensing image (HSI) is a key technology for fine feature information extraction and recognition. Aiming at the problems of the existing HSI classification network architecture being fixed and parameter redundant, and the failure to design an adaptive architecture from images, this paper proposed a Dedicated Network for HSI classification based on Multi-Objective evolutionary search (MODNet). In the proposed MODNet, the network test accuracy and parameter quantity are firstly simultaneously modeled to balance the parameter redundancy of the classification network. Discrete coding of the network architecture, corresponding to the different computational operators, initializes multiple network architectures for optimal search in the search space through the population based and the non-dominated ranking based on the multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA). The effectiveness was demonstrated through the experiment conducted on the WHU-Hi-Hanchuan dataset.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Hyperspectral Object Tracking: Leveraging Spectral Information Prompts and Spectral Scale-Aware Representation
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Under the constraint of limited training samples, achieving robust tracking of hyperspectral data with various target characteristics using a single network is challenging. To address this issue, firstly, we propose a Multi-Band hyperspectral object tracking algorithm based on Spectral Scale-Aware representation (SSAMB). This algorithm can adaptively perceive and capture object characteristics in hyperspectral data across different spectral scales. Secondly, inspired by the “prompt learning” paradigm, we propose a Hyperspectral Object Tracking network based on Spectral Information Prompts (SIPHOT). It aims to fully leverage the powerful tracking capability of the RGB-based model to alleviate the issue of limited training samples affecting the model’s generalization performance. Meanwhile, it can effectively utilize the “spectral dimension advantage” of hyperspectral data to enhance object tracking accuracy. The experimental results on the HOT2023 dataset demonstrate that the proposed SSAMB and SIPHOT trackers perform excellently on different spectral data, validating the effectiveness of our methods.

articleTitle: Harmful Algal Bloom (HAB) Detection Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks and Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: A total of 198 Sentinel-2 Level-2A datasets over a 13,000-acre reservoir in Virginia were used to determine if deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) could detect the presence of harmful algal blooms (HABs) – an event during which cyanobacteria replicate at abnormal rates and create toxins harmful to living organisms. The water collection campaign focused on over 45 sites throughout the lake and produced the bulk of the ground-truthed data. The Sentinel-2 datasets provided the spectral data used to match to laboratory spectral measurements. Finally, CNNs were used to learn and detect the spectral characteristics of HABs on remote sensing data. The proposed approach to the development of the CNN and the curating of the Sentinel-2 data showed that CNNs could detect harmful algal blooms with a 93% accuracy after at least 50 epochs.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Imaging Classification of Fungal Species Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) offers fast, non-destructive spectral data acquisition, overcoming the limitations of traditional methods. With the HSI technique we aim to improve the identification of fungal species, assisting in the timely diagnosis of fungal infections and automating unhealthy manual processes of microbiological products. This contribution centers on the differentiation of four distinct fungal species by leveraging HSI alongside supervised machine learning techniques, where we conduct comparisons between different classification approaches. After acquiring HSI captures of fungal samples in isolated colonies for each species, they were subjected to an appropriate pre-processing process, which included calibration, correction and application of signal filters. The highest accuracy of 97.12% was achieved by applying the multilayer perceptron (MLP). The results highlight the potential of machine learning methodology applied to HSI for clinical and microbiological environments as an alternative to time-consuming techniques in the work of differentiating fungal species.

articleTitle: Asymmetric-Scale Arbitrary Resolution Pansharpening CNN for Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Hyperspectral (HS) pansharpening seeks to fuse low spatial resolution HS (LRHS) images with corresponding panchromatic (PAN) images to obtain high spatial resolution HS (HRHS) images. Arbitrary resolution HS (ARHS) pansharpening, as an evolution of traditional HS pansharpening technique, can generate HS images with arbitrary spatial resolutions. However, existing ARHS pansharpening methods are not concerned about the situation of asymmetric scales. In this work, we propose an asymmetric-scale arbitrary resolution pansharpening convolution neural network (CNN), called ASAR-PNN for brevity, which can produce HS images with asymmetric scales in an adaptive way according to scale factors. Experiment results on a simulated HS dataset suggest the superiority of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Advancing Prisma Pansharpening: A Deep Learning Approach with Synthetic Data Pretraining and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Hyperspectral pansharpening has gained significant importance in recent years as hyperspectral systems have become more widely available. In order to generate an enhanced hyperspectral cube with improved spatial and spectral resolution, this technique fuses a panchromatic image with a hyperspectral cube. In this paper, we investigate the application of pansharpening to PRISMA data by proposing a novel training approach and deep learning model. To overcome the lack of ground truth data, we first leverage synthetic data, generated using AVIRIS-NG imagery, to pretrain the model in a supervised manner, enabling it to learn robust representations of spectral and spatial features. Subsequently, unsupervised transfer learning and PRISMA data are used to fine-tune the model and adapt it to the specific characteristics of the PRISMA sensor. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving promising pansharpening performances, paving the way for enhanced hyperspectral data analysis in various remote sensing applications.

articleTitle: Deep Fair Partition for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Over the last decade, hyperspectral images (HSIs) have attracted considerable attention in the remote sensing community, making HSI classification and segmentation a major concern. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely used in HSI classification and segmentation due to their effectiveness and efficiency in feature extraction and expression. However, traditional patch-wise classification methods may easily lead to information leakage, rendering overoptimistic results and making it imperative to address data leakage issues to ensure classification performance. In this paper, we propose a novel data partitioning strategy along with a lightweight, attention-aided CNN-based model for HSI classification without any information leakage. Not only does the proposed data partition method avoid information leakage, but it also generates balanced data splits even if the training samples are limited and datasets are imbalanced. Though our model only exploits spectral features instead of extracting spectral-spatial information, it is very effective and efficient since there is abundant spectral information; moreover, the spatial information is not easy to utilize effectively due to the limited availability of training samples and low spatial resolution in datasets. Experimental results, collected by applying the proposed novel data partitioning scheme and attention-aided CNN networks to three standard hyperspectral datasets, outperforms the state-of-the-art CNN-based models without any information leakage.

articleTitle: QECM-2: A novel visualization of the influence of Earth’s precession index variations on the insolation, precipitation, and photosynthetic activity experienced by equatorial regions
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: This investigation inquired the extent to which the decrease of the precession index—perihelion, eccentricity, and obliquity—of Earth impacts climate conditions in two stretches of latitudinal regions: 22.25° to 34.75° and -17.75° to -25.25°. Using the NASA POWER and Earth Observations databases, Earth’s decreasing precession index and the precipitation, insolation, and net primary productivity (NPP) of Morocco, Mexico, Botswana, and Brazil from 2000-2015 were analyzed. My results indicated that "precessional targets" experience contrasting precipitation and NPP trends to accepted global climate models that align with fluctuations in the angle of the received radiation. I derived four quasi-periodic mathematical models representing the kiloyear climate evolution and employed them in a 97.7% accurate C++ climate model (QECM-2) outputting a graphical visualization of the precipitation and productivity specific coordinates will experience 50 years into the future, building off of the current (2020) precipitation and NPP value of that region.

articleTitle: A Contrastive Learning Method for Multi-Label Predictors on Hyperspectral Images
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Self-supervised contrastive learning is increasingly acknowledged as an effective approach to mitigate the challenges posed by limited annotated data. We introduce a two-stage methodology that extends current approaches, targeting the downstream task of multi-label classification in hyperspectral remote-sensing imagery. In the initial stage, we employ a contrastive learning approach to train a base encoder and a projection neural network, thereby learning data patterns without relying on annotations. The effectiveness of the encoder is bolstered as it is guided by a contrastive loss function to maximize the similarity between the generated embeddings. In the second stage, we harness the power of the pre-trained encoder to channel its hidden representations into a multi-label classifier. Our empirical validation demonstrate that this method surpasses fully supervised alternatives. The observed improvements are attributed to the strategy of training the encoder alongside the classifier, thereby refining its adaptability to the feature space of the classifier.

articleTitle: A White-Box Workflow for the Prediction of Food Content From Near-Infrared Data Based on Fourier-Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: In this work we propose an white-box workflow for regression related tasks based on near-infrared data in the context of machine learning. The workflow consists of data pre-processing and dimension reduction through (inverse) Fourier-transformation and low-pass filtering of the spectra. Subsequently, a machine learning model shall be applied to predict food contents of the spectra and conclude the workflow. To yield recommendations, we test various standard models, as well as the iterative method of partial-least-squares and the recently proposed Regression (Sensitive) Neural Gas. We shall not only investigate performance aspects, but also discuss theoretical concepts, i.e. interpretability options offered by each model. We show that our pre-processing and reduction approach is able to achieve good results even for signal-to-noise ratio dependent models and that the Regression (Sensitive) Neural Gas offers rich options to gain insights into the data and the model results.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Band Selection based on Spectra Division and Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: In this paper, Spectra Division-based deep Convolutional Neural Network (SD-CNN) for hyperspectral band selection is proposed. The proposed method addresses the problems such as Hughes’ phenomena and the requirement of more storage space. In the proposed method, the bands of a given hyperspectral image are first grouped based on spectra division. Second, the wrapper method with the state-of-the-art pixel-wise deep learning-based spectral classifier such as 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) with sequential forward selection strategy is used to obtain a subset of bands of the original spectral bands that could suitably represent the hyperspectral image. The results of experiments conducted on two challenging hyperspectral datasets, such as Pavia University (PU) and Indian Pines (IP), and their comparison with the representative state-of- the-art wrapper-based spectral band selection methods substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed band selection method of SD-CNN. The OA, AA, and Kappa of SD-CNN have shown improvement of at least 1.05%, 2.74%, and 1.46%, respectively for the PU dataset, and those at least 5.35%, 3.98%, and 6.19%, respectively for the IP dataset over representative comparison methods.

articleTitle: SWUNet: Swin Transformer Based UNet for Hyperspectral Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: We introduce hyperspectral vision transformer: an architecture that leverages Swin Transformer as a backbone for HSI super-resolution task. While in RGB images a low-level vision problem encompasses estimating low-frequency structures and also reconstructing high frequency details. In addition to this, in HSI it becomes even more challenging due to the large number of spectral bands having high dimension and high correlation/redundancy between adjacent bands. This causes difficulty to super-resolve HSI. Many methods based on convolutional neural networks have been explored which resulted in various state-of-the-art (SOTA )results when extracting low-level concepts in an image. The attempts made with transformers show high quality performance on such tasks. In this paper, we propose a Unet inspired SWUNet transformer for hyperspectral image superresolution an encoder decoder structure with Swin transformer blocks. SWUNet consists of three parts: Convolutional extractor (for shallow features), Swin Transformer based encoder, Swin Transformer based decoder with a enhancing module (Pixel shuffle). This encoder-decoder ensures shifted window based self-attention in local windows as well as in cross-windows. This allows two varied window sets to capture attention along the spatial and spectral domain which expresses correlation for adjacent spectral efficiently for every spatial location. Experiments on two public HSI datasets express the strength of leveraging shifted windows in HSI.

articleTitle: Predicting Food Insecurity in Africa From Modis Imagery, Demographics, Economic Factors, Climate, and Supply Chain Information
publicationTitle: 2023 13th Workshop on Hyperspectral Imaging and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS)
abstract: Food insecurity in Africa is one of the major global-scale humanitarian disasters. The UN World Health Organization estimates that 37 million people in the horn of Africa are in acute hunger and describe the current situation as one of the worst hunger crises in the last 70 years. In this study we present a machine learning prediction using Gaussian processes and Bayesian model averaging to predict the probability and quantity of food insecurity for each country in Africa along with proposed locations for new transshipment nodes based on the current food supply chain. Additionally, we provide a taxonomy of the various types of predictor variables to infer importance of certain factors on food security. Our predictions are based on demographic, climate, environmental, financial, supply chain disruption, and remote sensing crop yield information, trained on historical food insecurity data. Proposed locations for additional transshipment locations is designed to optimize efficiency of the locations within the current supply chain. Results are shared publicly with a HTML interactive GIS.
